plan.planning_summary: This control axis tests thickness optimization on a fixed 20-layer HfO2/SiO2 alternating stack for dual-band UV-reflection/SWIR-transmission filtering. The hypothesis draws from recalled quarter-wave stack principles where optical path differences create constructive interference in reflection bands and destructive interference in transmission bands. Prior knowledge suggests ~30-50nm layers for UV blocking and ~100-150nm for SWIR pass, but exact values require optimization. This route uses no retrieved literature - all design choices come from the model's prior knowledge of thin-film optics.

routes.title: Thickness optimization on 20-layer HfO2/SiO2 alternating stack for UV-block/SWIR-pass filtering
routes.scientific_hypothesis: A 20-layer alternating HfO2/SiO2 stack with optimized individual thicknesses can simultaneously achieve high UV reflection (200-400nm) and high SWIR transmission (800-1500nm) on fused silica substrate, with performance improving as thickness perturbations explore wider bounds around the current best candidate.
routes.design_principle: Recalled thin-film interference theory: alternating high/low index layers create Bragg-like reflection bands where optical thickness equals quarter-wavelength multiples. UV blocking requires thinner layers (shorter wavelength), while SWIR transmission requires the stack to be anti-reflective at longer wavelengths. The refractive index contrast between HfO2 (~2.0-2.1 in visible) and SiO2 (~1.45-1.5) provides sufficient modulation for band separation.
routes.proposed_topology: Air | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | Fused Silica substrate (20 layers total, alternating starting with HfO2)
design_variables: Individual layer thicknesses for all 20 layers, with perturbation bounds of ±0.8 nm around the current best candidate's thickness vector
soft_objectives: Maximize target_score combining UV reflection and SWIR transmission
Keep all layers physically realizable (positive thickness, manufacturable range)
manufacturing_considerations: Total layer count fixed at 20 (within 30-layer limit)
All thicknesses should remain in 20-200nm range for practical deposition
Alternating sequence preserved for process simplicity
theory_basis: Recalled principle: quarter-wave stacks produce high reflection at wavelengths where optical thickness equals λ/4 multiples
Recalled principle: index contrast between HfO2 and SiO2 enables bandgap formation in reflection spectrum
Recalled rule of thumb: UV-blocking layers typically 25-50nm physical thickness for 200-400nm band
Recalled expectation: SWIR transmission improves when stack appears optically thin at 800-1500nm wavelengths
expected_advantages: Fixed topology isolates thickness as the only optimization variable
20 layers provides sufficient degrees of freedom within manufacturing constraints
Alternating sequence is deposition-friendly and reduces process complexity
Wider perturbation bounds (±0.8nm vs ±0.5nm) may escape local optima causing round-to-round oscillation
known_risks: Uncertain whether 20 layers is optimal vs 24 or 28 layers - this route does not test layer count
Recalled refractive indices may differ from actual catalog values at UV wavelengths - HfO2 absorption in deep UV is uncertain from memory
Exact quarter-wave thickness calculation depends on dispersion data I have not verified
Wider perturbation bounds may produce non-manufacturable thickness variations if optimizer overshoots
What would settle this: look up HfO2 extinction coefficient at 200-300nm, verify SiO2 dispersion in SWIR band
routes.execution_request_english: Optimize a 20-layer planar dielectric stack on fused silica substrate with air incidence. Materials: alternating hfo2 and SiO2 (Rodriguez-de_Marcos) layers, starting with hfo2 adjacent to air. Design variables: all 20 individual layer thicknesses, initialized from the current best candidate thickness vector with perturbation bounds of ±0.8 nm. Wavelength bands: maximize reflection at 200-400 nm, maximize transmission at 800-1500 nm. Normal incidence, unpolarized light. Total layers fixed at 20. Use gradient_thickness optimizer. Keep all thicknesses positive and within 20-200 nm range.
routes.revision_reason: Continuation of control route with increased perturbation bounds from ±0.5 nm to ±0.8 nm as directed by feedback, anchored to current best candidate thickness vector to maintain focus on validated high-performance region while granting optimizer sufficient degrees of freedom to bypass shallow optical-path barriers.

plan.knowledge_source_disclosure: This route was planned from the model's own prior knowledge alone. No Semantic Scholar query was issued, no retrieved paper reached the prompt, and no method-research report was supplied -- neither for the initial plan nor for any continuation round. It is the control arm of a controlled comparison against the literature-grounded routes, and its evidence-id allowlist is empty by construction.
unresolved_decisions: Whether 20 layers is the optimal count vs 24 or 28 - this route holds layer count fixed
Exact HfO2 extinction coefficient at 200-300 nm wavelengths - recalled as low but not verified
Whether fused silica substrate dispersion significantly affects SWIR band performance - assumed negligible from memory
plan.stop_if_all_routes_fail: If this control route cannot exceed target_score of 0.80 after perturbation bound adjustment, the fixed alternating topology may be fundamentally limited for this dual-band requirement and a different stack sequence would be needed.

expected_observations: best_target_score should rise or remain stable compared to iteration_12 best of 0.8279 if wider bounds help escape local optima
best_target_score should not fall by more than 0.01 if the current region is near-optimal
tightest_margin should not fall across rounds if physical validity is maintained
valid_candidates count should remain at 9 if perturbation bounds stay within feasible region
If best_target_score oscillates without improvement over 3 consecutive rounds, the ±0.8 nm bounds may be too wide for this topology
stop_conditions: if best_target_score improves by less than 1e-3 against the historical best for two consecutive rounds, treat the axis as exhausted, stop and keep the current best
if valid_candidates falls below 5 for two consecutive rounds, reduce perturbation bounds to ±0.5 nm and continue
if tightest_margin falls below 0.30 for two consecutive rounds, constrain thickness range more tightly and continue

selector_prompt.system:
You are the internal material-dataset selector inside a scientific TMM
harness. This is not route planning and you must not redesign the route.
Return exactly one JSON object and no markdown:
{"selections":[{"request_id":"material_01","selected_rank":1,"provider":"rii_sqlite","dataset_id":562,"reason":"..."}]}

The user question is authoritative. Each request contains candidates already
retrieved from the local MaterialRegistry and sorted by three equal physical
metrics: target-band coverage, n/k completeness, and sampling density. Rank 1
is the most physically reliable candidate; lower rank means less reliable.
Choose exactly one candidate from the supplied list for every request. Never
invent, rename, or edit a provider or dataset_id. The selected_rank must point
to the selected array element, and provider/dataset_id must copy that element.

Material identity, stoichiometry, explicit material state/preparation, and an
explicit requested source are hard constraints. A candidate with
formula_exact=false or semantic_match=same_element_family is not an allowed
substitute for a formula request. SiO is not SiO2, even if the SiO2 candidate
has better physical coverage. When several candidates satisfy the hard
constraints, select the highest-ranked one (usually rank 1). If no candidate
satisfies them, return selected_rank:null, provider:null, dataset_id:null and
reason:"needs_confirmation" for that request.
